messages:
Maya (Customer): Hey team — hitting an issue where the client starts getting tokens over SSE and then drops mid-stream when the phone switches from 5G to WiFi. Partial output is delivered, and the client never reconnects properly. Happening on iOS app only.
Sam (Support): Thanks Maya — can you share a repro (steps + logs)? Also which SDK/version and whether you use a proxy or keep-alive pings?
Maya (Customer): App SDK v1.4.2 (swift). We see the SSE connection close with code 1006 sometimes. Repro steps: 1) Start a long streamed completion (30s+), 2) while streaming flip from cellular -> wifi (house AP), 3) often the stream ends with partial tokens. Happens ~4/10 tries. Logs below.
Maya (Customer): ```
[INFO] SSE connected to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
[T=12.3s] Received tokens: "The quick brown fox ..."
[T=15.8s] Network changed: 5G -> WiFi
[T=15.9s] TCP FIN
[T=16.0s] SSE connection closed (code=1006)
[T=16.0s] client reconnect attempt 1 -> fails: TLS handshake error
[T=16.4s] No further tokens
```
Sam (Support): Good, that 1006 + TLS handshake fail on reconnect is helpful. Does the SDK attempt an idempotent resume (stream id / offset)?
Maya (Customer): Not currently — we just re-open a fresh SSE with same request body. The server will re-run generation from scratch, but client discards duplicates. We expected the server to send the rest but it doesn't resume mid-queue.
Luis (Repro): I can reproduce locally on an emulator with a flaky network toggle. Observed same sequence: FIN then immediate reconnect fails due to client TCP stack still transitioning.
Alex (Mobile Eng): On iOS the URLSession SSE wrapper acts weird across network handoffs. We also saw TLS session caching can be lost when switching WiFi networks which causes handshake stalls. Are you using keepalive/heartbeats from the server to detect stale connections?
Sam (Support): @Alex any recommended quick client mitigations?
Alex (Mobile Eng): Two things to try immediately: (1) implement exponential reconnect with jitter and check the TLS session reuse flags; (2) when detecting network change do a short delay (~200-400ms) before reconnect so the OS finishes closing previous sockets. Also add an application-level resume token in the stream request so the server can continue from last token.
Ingrid (SRE): From server side, we saw a cluster metric spike at the same minute — many short-lived SSEs causing extra cold-start overhead. Server currently treats every new stream as fresh; no resume API. We can add an intermediate short-term cache keyed by customer stream id to allow resume up to last KV cache checkpoint for ~30s.
Sam (Support): Proposal: short-term plan for customer is client patch + server config tweak. Client: add a backoff + 250ms post-network-change delay and send stream_id header. Server: enable 30s resume cache for that customer and increase SSE keepalive to 15s to reduce false positives.
Maya (Customer): That sounds good. Can you outline exact headers/body we should send for the stream_id?
Luis (Repro): Use a unique UUID per attempt that persists across reconnects for the same logical request, e.g.:
```
POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Stream-Id: 9b1c2f6a-...

{ "model": "rwd-stream-1", "prompt": "tell me a long story...", "resume_from": 0 }
```
Sam (Support): Also include a client-side last_token_index so if you got 12 tokens you send resume_from=12 on reconnect. Server will try to emit the rest and will dedupe overlaps.
Alex (Mobile Eng): Quick client code sketch (swift):
```swift
// onNetworkChange:
DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now()+0.25) { startSSE(streamId: uuid, resumeFrom: lastIndex) }
// reconnect logic: backoff with jitter, max retries 5
```
Ingrid (SRE): We're going to flip a config on the staging cluster to enable a 30s resume cache and higher keepalive. I'll post logs once done. @deploy-bot will record the change.
deploy-bot: Configuration change applied to staging: sse_resume_cache_ttl=30s, sse_keepalive_interval=15s.
Ingrid (SRE): Staging test: toggled network on an iOS testbed, stream resumed and continued after reconnect, server emitted remaining tokens and deduped the overlapping token.
Maya (Customer): Great — will try the client delay + stream_id change once our mobile eng pushes a patch. Any other pitfalls?
Luis (Repro): Watch out for clients that drop cookies/headers on reconnect; also check proxy timeouts if customers are behind corp proxies — they can drop mid-stream and break resume.
Sam (Support): Final TL;DR for Maya: (1) Mobile eng adds 250ms delay after network-change + backoff reconnects, (2) send X-Redwood-Stream-Id and resume_from index, (3) we'll enable 30s resume cache and higher keepalive on your customer shard. Should reduce the mid-stream data loss.
Maya (Customer): Thanks folks. We'll ship a 1.4.3 quick client update and report back. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :raised_hands:
Alex (Mobile Eng): If you can ship a debug build with verbose network logs, ping me — I'll correlate with our staging traces.
Ingrid (SRE): Marking this as "working on fix" — follow-up message when patch rolled to prod.
Sam (Support): Closing loop after Maya confirms. If anything reappears we'll open an incident.
